items.title: Elden Ring A24 Movie: First Details, Budget Tease Epic Fantasy Adventure
items.content:
Bandai Namco Entertainment Add SlashFilm on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover One of the most-anticipated movies currently in the pipeline is undoubtedly A24's "Elden Ring." An adaptation of the best-selling game of the same name from Bandai Namco and FromSoftware, it's going to be a big movie, and the recently revealed budget and first details have confirmed as much.

According to Deadline , A24 will handle theatrical distribution in North America, but they are selling other rights to buyers around the world. Amazon, for example, has purchased some overseas streaming rights. But the bigger detail is that the report confirms the budget to be at least $175 million, and likely closer to $200 million. A24 knows its cult following won't cut it anymore at the box office , so they're taking bigger bets. This is by far their biggest bet to date.

The "Elden Ring" movie adaptation comes from modern sci-fi legend Alex Garland , who previously directed "Annihilation" and "Ex-Machina." Specific plot details are still largely being kept under wraps. The game itself takes place after the Elden Ring is shattered, focusing on an exiled, nameless Tarnished who returns to the Lands Between, battling demigods and monsters to claim the title of Elden Lord.

Garland wrote the script for the movie. It turns out the director struggled with the same "Elden Ring" video game boss you did , so he's a real fan with a real understanding of what he's tackling. As for the script, it's said to be a whopping 180 pages, meaning it could push three hours. Most plot details are being kept secret, but we do know new some info, which you can read below.

Bandai Namco Entertainment A24 is flying members of its team to international buyers for them to read the script with the employee present. What we do know is that Kit Connor ("Heartstopper") is the movie's protagonist and it's said to be "faithful" to the game. Without specifics, the report notes there are "battles between his character and impressive monsters and dragons." Most intriguing of all? Parts of the script are apparently being held back from buyers in "to avoid spoilers and increase intrigue." The studio is not letting secrets get out.

Aside from the lack of plot details, the "Elden Ring" movie has one of the best casts ever for a video game adaptation . Cailee Spaeny, Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, Ruby Cruz, and Nick Offerman are all on board.

For A24, the stakes could not be higher. The studio has been making more expensive movies as of late, such as "Marty Supreme" ($70 million budget), but this is on another level. Having Alex Garland at the helm makes sense. His 2024 movie "Civil War" became A24's second movie to ever hit $100 million at the box office . But a movie of this size needs to make hundreds of millions. It's a big gamble.

The studio is mitigating a lot of that risk by selling off various rights but, ultimately, it's a $200 million investment that has to pay off. Fortunately, the game sold over 36 million copies and is one of the most acclaimed titles in recent gaming history. The audience is there if Garland delivers the goods.

The "Elden Ring" movie is set to hit theaters on March 3, 2028.

As we reported earlier this spring, FromSoftware's hit action RPG Elden Ring is getting a movie adaptation. While the plot remains a mystery, we already know that several big names are involved . Now we also have an idea of how much production studio A24 might be willing to spend. According to industry publication Deadline , the movie could cost between $175 million and $200 million to produce, with the budget reportedly leaning toward the upper end of that range. That could make Elden Ring the most expensive video game movie of all time.

ⓘ FromSoftware The world of Elden Ring is a dark fantasy realm filled with towering castles, mysterious ruins and dangerous monsters. Since the Elden Ring was shattered, the realm has descended into chaos, with powerful demigods fighting for supremacy. (Pictured: Official Elden Ring artwork.) For comparison, the 2016 Warcraft movie had a production budget of around $160 million, while the Uncharted movie from 2022 cost approximately $120 million. The strongest contender for the title of most expensive video game adaptation is 2010's Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time , which reportedly cost $200 million to make and is widely considered the most expensive video game movie to date. Whether that investment was worthwhile is debatable, especially considering the movie's poor reviews . If the Elden Ring movie ends up costing slightly more than expected, which isn't unusual for Hollywood productions, it could take the title outright. Even if it simply reaches the upper end of its reported budget, it could at least tie with Prince of Persia .

One major reason for the substantial budget could be the movie's length. According to Deadline, the screenplay is reportedly around 180 pages long, suggesting that the Elden Ring movie could run for approximately three hours. The world of Elden Ring ( PS5 version currently $40 on Amazon ) also offers plenty of opportunities for elaborate visual effects and large-scale set pieces. Vast landscapes, monstrous enemies and spectacular battles could easily consume a significant portion of the production budget. The involvement of Industrial Light & Magic, one of Hollywood's most renowned visual effects studios, further supports that assumption.

items.title: Elden Ring movie's 180-page script hints at three-hour adventure through the Lands Between
items.summary: Alex Garland's ambitious adaptation of Elden Ring is set to become A24's biggest film production yet.
items.content:
All News Filming for the movie has wrapped up (Image: FromSoftware).

{" "} Elden Ring movie's 180-page script hints at three-hour adventure through the Lands Between .iframe-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .img-media {width: 100%;aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} .a-img-media {aspect-ratio: auto 16/9;} Alex Garland's ambitious adaptation of Elden Ring is set to become A24's biggest film production yet. The upcoming live-action adaptation of FromSoftware's acclaimed action RPG Elden Ring could be nearly three hours long, according to new details surrounding the highly anticipated film.

According to an exclusive report by Deadline on Tuesday (27 October), the script spans at least 180 pages, including visuals, suggesting that the film could approach the three-hour mark. However, its official runtime has yet to be confirmed.

The A24 production, written and directed by Alex Garland, has plenty of material to draw from. With the sheer scale of the Lands Between, its sprawling lore, and its formidable bosses, there's certainly enough to explore in a lengthy adaptation.

While much of the film's plot remains under wraps, Deadline's report has revealed more details about what players can expect when Elden Ring makes its way to the big screen. Kit Connor, who was previously announced as part of the film's star-studded cast , will take on the role of the protagonist, whose journey will involve battles against fearsome creatures and dragons.

Boss battles are among Elden Ring's defining features, with players facing everything from monstrous creatures to powerful demigods and legendary dragons. Deadline did not identify which enemies will appear in the adaptation, leaving fans guessing whether familiar bosses such as Starscourge Radahn, Malenia, or Dragonlord Placidusax will make it to the big screen.

A24 has gone to considerable lengths to keep the film's story under wraps, even having staff accompany potential international buyers as they read the screenplay and withholding certain sections to prevent spoilers. However, keeping everything a secret has proven difficult, especially with filming taking place at real-world locations. Earlier this year, leaked footage and images from the film's London sets surfaced online, showing what appeared to be Queen Marika, the Dung Eater, and references to familiar locations such as Leyndell, Stormveil, and Raya Lucaria.

Meanwhile, the film's budget is estimated at between US$175 million and US$200 million, making it A24's most expensive production to date. Amazon MGM Studios has also secured pay-1 streaming rights in numerous international markets, although A24 remains responsible for financing the film. According to Deadline, filming has already wrapped, with post-production now underway alongside visual effects company Industrial Light & Magic.

The Elden Ring movie is scheduled to arrive in cinemas and IMAX on 3 March, 2028.

items.title: Review – The Relic: First Guardian
items.summary: More like the smel-lic, am I right?
items.content:
Action RPGs are actually one of my favourite genres of game, but finding the good ones is more difficult than it should be sometimes. You’ve got games like Diablo , Elden Ring , Mass Effect , and The Witcher to compete with. So having the chance to check out a new one, The Relic: First Guardian , I couldn’t say no, simply because I would love something that is gonna grab my attention for a longer playthrough like this genre tends to offer.

The Relic: First Guardian , takes place in a world destroyed by the Great Relic. You’re, as the name suggests, the guardian of the relic, but you have amnesia and can’t remember what your goal is. Not very convenient, isn’t it? You follow a mysterious voice around the world, collect shards of the relic, seek to honor the voices of those who came before you, save the world, happy days.

Somebody call 911! Shawty fire burning on the dance floor!

The biggest difference from the majority of ARPGs is the fact there’s no traditional levelling system. There’s no XP granted from defeating enemies, besides money. There’s actually no point to defeating enemies as it stands in this current system. Now, money can be looked at the same way as Souls/Ruins in a way. Gold is used to buy weapon, health, and stamina upgrades, so it’s a semi-familiar feeling to Soulslike fans.

One key difference in this respect is none of it is lost if you die, which means no corpse runs to make sure you don’t lose anything. Realistically, there’s actually no negative to dying, it’s just more of an inconvenience. Although, if you look around for the runestones where you save your progress (basically this game’s bonfires), there are plenty around so you’re never far from the action. This further takes away an semblance of challenge.

I found another site of gra… Wait, wrong game.

The Relic: First Guardian keeps most situations to one on one combat. There aren’t a lot of spots, unless you choose to run through everything, where multiple enemies will attack you at the same time. There’s essentially two types of enemies, if you really want to dumb it down. The ones that get staggered and the ones that don’t. The enemies that get staggered are obviously incredibly easy, you hit them and they don’t swing back. Obviously, the types that don’t take a bit more effort because the recovery time after each attack is fairly unforgiving. Unlike a game like Dark Souls , you can’t seem to dodge through attacks, so you need to aim to dodge out of range.

You also have an ability you can use to help damage enemies, starting with a fireball. I found this to be incredibly frustrating because half the time I pressed L and R to use it, it didn’t seem to want to activate, it was just making me aim in the middle of fighting an enemy or a boss and throwing me off. On that note, I know after Elden Ring , saying this game has 80+ bosses is nothing, but between the rather unforgiving recovery time, and what feels like no I-frames, even the simplest boss can be a little frustrating.

So what’s the verdict? The Relic: First Guardian has some systems that are clearly borrowed from other ARPG games, but simply not incorporated very well. It wants to play like a Soulslike, but doesn’t have the fluidity. It wants to have weapon specific gear builds, but everything is based around the weapon skill trees and not finding upgraded gear. There’s next to no reason to refight enemies, and outside of a little frustration there’s no penalty to dying so you may as well just run through areas. End of the day, there are a lot of games that do every mechanic The Relic: First Guardian does, but better, so it’s not exactly worth the time investment.

Far from the best looking game available on Switch 2. It’s not the worst looking game you could play, but I can’t think of many that offer less visually Gameplay: 4.0

Wants to be baby’s first Soulslike. Wants to be baby’s first ARPG. Misses the mark on everything it’s aiming to be, which just creates a mess of gameplay mechanics. Sound: 2.5

There’s almost nothing to say here. The voice acting doesn’t sound genuine, the ambient sound doesn’t make the world feel alive. Fun Factor: 3.0

There haven’t been a lot of games this year I’m actively going to avoid playing more. This is one of them though. Final Verdict: 3.5 The Relic: First Guardian is available now on Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S.

A copy of The Relic: First Guardian was provided by the publisher .

items.title: Elden Ring Movie Runtime Could Reach Nearly 3 Hours
items.summary: A few new details on the story for A24’s Elden Ring movie have emerged, including its possible runtime. And, if that remains the case, it’s going to be epic.
items.content:
A few new details on the story for A24’s Elden Ring movie have emerged, including its possible runtime. And, if that remains the case, it’s going to be epic.

Deadline reports that writer-director Alex Garland’s screenplay , based on FromSoftware’s acclaimed fantasy video game, “runs to at least 180 pages with visuals, implying the movie could push towards three hours. While plot details are largely being kept under wraps, we understand that in-demand Heartstopper actor [Kit] Connor is the protagonist and the ‘faithful’ film will follow his journey. There are said to be battles between his character and impressive monsters and dragons.”

The site also claims that A24 is allowing potential international buyers to read Garland’s Elden Ring script, but only with a studio staff member present (for security reasons, naturally).

It was reported last week that the Elden Ring movie is the most expensive film A24 has ever produced – Deadline’s report today pegs it at “between $175 million-200 million, but closer to the latter” – and now comes word that the studio, which fully financed the film, is looking to mitigate some of that risk by bringing in a partner with very deep pockets: Amazon.

According to Deadline, Amazon MGM Studios has now acquired “a bunch of international pay-1 streaming rights... The pact is understood to cover a large number of international markets, and sources speculate to us that it is easily worth tens of millions of dollars. We hear the deal could also potentially lead to interesting activations on Amazon’s Twitch platform.”

The film’s huge price tag makes Elden Ring one of the most expensive films that will be shopped at next month’s American Film Market, which touts itself as “the premier marketplace for the acquisition, development, financing, and distribution of independent film, television, and premium content for audiences worldwide.”

Potential buyers at AFM will reportedly be treated to an Elden Ring movie presentation of some kind, including possibly seeing the very first footage from this highly-anticipated film.

After some set photos made their way online , Elden Ring wrapped filming in July and is scheduled to open in theaters on March 3, 2028.

In addition to Kit O’Connor, the cast includes Ben Whishaw, Cailee Spaeny, Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, Nick Offerman and Peter Serafinowicz .

Are you excited by the prospect of a three-hour Elden Ring movie? Let us know in the comments.

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

items.title: Amazon Scores a Win on George RR Martin's New Fantasy Epic Based on 30-Million-Copy Video Game
items.summary: Amazon is now backing the epic fantasy blockbuster based on the video game written by the author of Game of Thrones.
items.content:
Image via HBO / Courtesy MovieStillsDB Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Jamie Lovett Published Oct 27, 2026, 11:44 AM EDT Jamie Lovett is a graduate of MTSU's Journalism program who followed his lifelong passion for comics and related media into a career writing about pop culture. He has over a decade of experience writing about television, movies, comics, video games, and more, and recently co-founded the comics-focused newsletter/site Weird City Media. Sign in to your CBR account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap George R.R. Martin's writing has already reshaped fantasy television with Game of Thrones , and it may stand to do the same for fantasy movies. A24 is bringing its Elden Ring adaptation, its most expensive movie ever, to the American Film Market, but Amazon MGM has already gotten a piece of the action.

According to Deadline , the Elden Ring movie has a budget of $175–200 million, making it the most expensive movie ever brought to market. Deadline also reports that, ahead of the market, Amazon MGM has secured several international pay-1 streaming rights to the movie in a deal speculated to be worth tens of millions of dollars.

Rumors also suggest cross-promotion with the Amazon-owned game-streaming platform Twitch. That makes sense for a movie based on a video game that has sold more than 30 million copies.

Alex Garland ( Annihilation , Ex Machina ) both wrote and directed Elden Ring , which is now in post-production. Kit Connor stars in the fantasy movie. He's joined by Ben Whishaw, Cailee Spaeny, Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, Ruby Cruz, and Nick Offerman.

Details about the Elden Ring movie's plot remain closely guarded. The game is set in a fantasy realm called the Lands Between, ruled by several demigods. Previously, the immortal Queen Marika ruled and guarded the Elden Ring, a powerful force that physically embodies the concept of order. After Marika shattered the Elden Ring and disappeared, her demigod children began fighting over the Ring's pieces in a war called the Shattering. Each demigod possesses a shard, or Great Rune, which empowers and corrupts them. Players control one of the Tarnished, exiles from the Lands Between. They return after the Shattering. As a Tarnished, the player travels the realm to repair the Elden Ring and claim the title of Elden Lord.

Elden Ring was developed by FromSoftware, known for its punishingly challenging fantasy games like Dark Souls ​​​​​. Miyazaki, creator of that series, directed Elden Ring and wrote the in-game narrative. FromSoftware reached out to Martin to write the game's backstory , hoping to create a more engaging narrative than in the studio's previous games. Bandai Namco published the game, which was released in 2022 and became an instant hit, earning near-unanimous critical acclaim.

Elden Ring's Starscourge Radahn vs Malenia Image via FromSoftware A24 is looking to grow beyond its reputation as a fan-favorite purveyor of quirky indie movies and to compete with the bigger studios on blockbuster ground. Elden Ring could be the movie that gets them there. It's based on an already popular intellectual property; it has a proven director and writer behind it, Martin's name attached, and it exists within a popular genre.

Reports suggest a sequel is already being considered, assuming A24's big bet pays off . It's still a big gamble, though, especially considering the massive budget.

The Elden Ring movie is slated for theatrical release on March 3, 2028.

10 Adventure Video Games Without a Single Flaw
items.summary: Uncharted 4: A Thief's End, Red Dead Redemption 2, and The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild are among the best, flawless adventure video games.
items.content:
elden ring Image via FromSoftware Add Collider on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Diego Pineda Pacheco Published Oct 26, 2026, 7:21 AM EDT Diego Pineda has been a devout storyteller his whole life. He has self-published a fantasy novel and a book of short stories, and is actively working on publishing his second novel. A lifelong fan of watching movies and talking about them endlessly, he writes reviews and analyses on his Instagram page dedicated to cinema, and occasionally on his blog. His favorite filmmakers are Andrei Tarkovsky and Charlie Chaplin . He loves modern Mexican cinema and thinks it's tragically underappreciated. Other interests of Diego's include reading, gaming, roller coasters, writing reviews on his Letterboxd account (username: DPP_reviews), and going down rabbit holes of whatever topic he's interested in at any given point. Sign in to your Collider account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The adventure genre has always been one of video gaming's most foundational pillars, having provided several titles that are often praised as some of the greatest in the medium's history . These are games all about allowing players to explore, solve puzzles, and interact with the environment. Whether they're combined with action elements or purely about adventure, it's a genre that's as timeless as video games themselves.

From modern action-adventure masterpieces like Uncharted 4: A Thief's End to foundational classics like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , there are plenty of adventure games that are great, but only a handful that are truly devoid of any substantial flaws. These are all must-play titles for gaming fans, and could potentially be phenomenal introductions to the adventure genre for the uninitiated.

Nathan Drake and Victor Sullivan in Uncharted 4: A Thief's End Image via Sony Computer Entertainment In 2007, Uncharted: Drake's Fortune proved that Naughty Dog was able to make cinematic, surprisingly mature action-adventure games unlike anything else they had delivered before. From there, the Uncharted franchise immediately became one of Sony's flagship IPs, but no one had ever seen anything quite like Uncharted 4: A Thief's End .

Promoted right off the bat as the final chapter in Nathan Drake's story, Uncharted 4 was a massive pop-cultural event which still feels delightfully modern a decade after its launch. Often ranked as the very best Uncharted game , it has an absolutely perfect balance between fluid traversal and refined combat mechanics . It's fun, it's action-packed, it's impeccably written, and it's the best possible way that Nathan's story could have possibly come to a close.

Ellie and Joel in The Last of Us Image via Naughty Dog Following the tremendous success of their first three Uncharted titles, Naughty Dog wanted to prove that they could take things even further when it came to telling powerfully cinematic, gritty, and mature stories through the gaming medium. Enter The Last of Us , one of the most universally loved games since 2000 , a blockbuster release that completely re-defined and revolutionized the survival horror genre.

On the one hand, you have the wonderfully complex and layered story, led by two of the most fascinating and endearing main characters in the history of gaming. Add to that some terrifyingly immersive gameplay, where every resource counts and every movement must be carefully thought-out; as well as some truly visceral and weighty combat, and you get one of the most groundbreaking games of the 2010s .

Scarred monster hunter Geralt of Rivera stands against a tree on a sunlit day with his sword holstered over his shoulder in 'The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt' (2015). Image via CD Projekt Red For many years, Polish writer Andrzej Sapkowski 's The Witcher books remained popular mostly just in Eastern Europe. It wouldn't be until the arrival of CD Projekt Red's game of the same title in 2007 that the franchise would smash its way into the mainstream . Likewise, it wouldn't be until the arrival of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt that this IP would truly cement itself as a pop culture sensation.

One of the best sword-and-sorcery games of all time , The Witcher 3 is one of the most sprawling open-world action-adventure RPGs the world has ever seen. With a level of narrative depth not often seen in the genre, including a myriad of side quests that manage to all feel deeply meaningful, it really has aged as one of the most important dark fantasy video games in the medium's history.

A village in Skyrim Image via Bethesda Softworks As great as they are, the first four titles in The Elder Scrolls series have dated mechanics and steep learning curves that make them not-all-that-welcoming to fantasy RPG newbies. The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim , on the other hand, is one of the best fantasy video games for beginners , a masterpiece that was widely acclaimed as one of the greatest video games ever made immediately upon hitting store shelves.

A decade and a half later, Skyrim still tends to be in the conversation whenever people talk about the greatest action-adventure games in history. It should be particularly appealing for those who prefer action-adventure titles that lean far more toward adventure than action, seeing as this is perhaps the ultimate sandbox of player freedom and agency. The level of player freedom and roleplaying potential that Skyrim allows for is still unmatched all these many years later.

Mario and a Luma in Super Mario Galaxy Image via Nintendo It would in no way be an understatement to say that 1985's Super Mario Bros. is one of the most groundbreaking video games of the 20th century. Eleven years later, Nintendo's poster boy made the jump to 3D, and things were never the same again. For the Wii generation, Nintendo knew that they needed to go all-out with Mario's newest adventure in the third dimension, and that's precisely where Super Mario Galaxy comes in.

Still widely remembered not only as one of the best Mario games of all time , but as one of the greatest video games of all time in general, Super Mario Galaxy is a genuine masterclass in level design and innovation. The mere act of moving Mario around and experiencing the stunning gravity mechanics is one of sheer joy, resulting in one of the most re-playable games Nintendo has thus far made.

Elden Ring Image via FromSoftware Whether George R. R. Martin will ever finish his Song of Ice and Fire book series remains to be seen, but at least he's keeping busy. He co-wrote Elden Ring with Hidetaka Miyakazi , and under Miyakazi and Yui Tanimura 's direction, this became one of the best video games released since 2020 . FromSoftware's Souls games have long been some of the greatest action RPG titles of all time, but never had a Souls game had a sense of adventure as rich as Elden Ring 's.

Without losing a single ounce of the depth, tension, atmosphere, of challenge that has always made their games successes.

items.title: PC users get dose of PS1 nostalgia with free Elden Ring meets Resident Evil taster
items.content:
Gamers nostalgic for something that resembles the early PlayStation days should look no further than False Oath.

Resident Evil fans are going to love this new PC exclusive, as it’s exactly what we’d imagine a game like Elden Ring would look like had it launched for the OG PlayStation.

As a console player, I’m horrendously jealous of the PC users, now more than ever after seeing the rumoured price for Xbox Project Helix .

Video game graphics are constantly improving and as such, the price of hardware is skyrocketing. Part of me wishes I’d just caved and bought a PC back in the day.

I’m even more jealous of PC users though after trying the False Oath demo on my Steam Deck.

Developed by Daniel Almenara and Nytelynn, False Oath is an upcoming Steam game that pays homage to PS1 games like Resident Evil , Dino Crisis, and more.

The synopsis reads: “ False Oath is a retro-style survival horror game set in a medieval era. A deadly plague spreads across the kingdom. Search for a cure before it’s too late.”

After looking at the screenshots and gameplay footage, you can tell the FromSoftware vibes are strong with this one. It’s very Kings Field -esque, but it’s exactly the type of game I’d picture in my head if you told me to imagine the likes of Elden Ring , Dark Souls or Demon Souls as a PS1 game.

It’s got a retro eeriness I haven’t seen since Crow Country , and it stands out from other games in the genre. I’m honestly surprised the idea hasn’t been done sooner.

False Oath is due to launch in Q1 of 2027 exclusively for PCs, but in the meantime, you can play a free demo to get a taste of what’s to come.

Despite Steam yielding no answer on whether the demo would work on Steam Deck, I threw caution to the wind and gave it a go anyway.

It didn’t work flawlessly, but it did the trick for some first impressions of the story, world design, and general gameplay. Hopefully when the full-game releases, it’ll be optimised for the Steam Deck.

From my own experience, I’d confidently say this is a game for me, and again that’s speaking as a huge fan of both Resident Evil and FromSoftware games. This scratches my itch for more modernised retro throwbacks .

It has that authentic clunkiness you’d expect from a game like this, and if the visuals weren’t so crisp, I’d have been fully convinced that this was some sort of long-lost PS1 game.

items.content:
The roar of the Red Lion echoes to the heavens.

He built his might out of love and loyalty, an unstoppable force that bade the stars to halt at the cry of a true champion. And in the Wailing Dunes, the loyalty he shared with others freed him from a fate worse than death. Now, the power of this greatest of Carian generals can rest in the palm of your hand. Standing 12 cm (4.7 in) tall, Starscourge Radahn is stylized figure that features simple articulation, interchangeable left- and right-hand parts that hold his Starscourge Greatsword, his detachable scrawny steed, and a dedicated display stand. Produced with the super-deformed proportions of the FIGURARTS Mini series, Starscourge Radahn is molded from quality PVC and ABS with exact attention to detail paid even at this miniature size. His golden armor, his raging snarl, even the gravity crests on his blades can be made out with perfect clarity. items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

*This products are available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

Note: After obtaining any Spectral Steed Attire, the option to change the spectral steed’s appearance will be added to the Site of Grace menu.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.
